title: TRUST configuration
description: Targets, safety limits and probe definitions for a TRUST run. Stores env var NAMES, never secret values — secrets belong in .env.

extends.description: Path to a config this one inherits from, relative to this file. The child overrides only what it declares; arrays replace rather than merge.

name.description: Assessment name, used in report filenames and titles.

environment.description: dev | staging | uat. Values matching prod/production/live are refused unless safety.productionOverride is set.

architecture.description: Optional free text rendered in the report's Architecture Under Test box.

limitations.description: Caveats to surface in the report's Limitations callout.

probes.description: Org-specific probe modules. Paths resolve against this file's directory first, then the working directory.

allowedHosts.description: Bare hostnames the harness may contact. This list is the technical boundary of the engagement — a request to anything else is refused before it leaves the process.

safety.description: Guards that make the harness incapable of harming the target.

maxRequests.description: A number caps the whole run; an object caps per profile, with an optional default.

budgets.description: Per-suite request caps, so one long sweep cannot exhaust the run before later suites execute.

allowDenialTests.description: Permit a mutation that is expected to be REFUSED, without enabling writes generally. If the target accepts it, that acceptance is the finding.

productionOverride.description: Required to target production. Set only with written authorisation for that specific system.

auth.description: Declarative credential acquisition. Strategies are resolved once before probes run; a section references one by name ("tokenA": "userA") instead of naming an env var.

type.description: static: a bearer token from the environment. cognito-srp: USER_SRP_AUTH, so no plaintext-password grant has to be enabled. cognito-identity-pool: exchange an ID token for temporary AWS credentials. sigv4: sign with AWS keys.

exportAs.description: Env var this credential is cached in and written to by `trust tokens`. Default TRUST_TOKEN_<NAME>.

scheme.description: Authorization scheme. Default Bearer; "" sends the raw token.

clientSecretEnv.description: Env var NAME holding the client secret.

passwordEnv.description: Env var NAME holding the password. Never the password itself.

tokenEnv.description: static only — env var NAME holding the token.

idTokenFrom.description: Name of another strategy whose ID token is exchanged.

service.description: SigV4 service, e.g. execute-api, s3, bedrock.

endpoint.description: Override the IdP endpoint. It must be in targets.allowedHosts — acquisition is guarded like any other request.

tokens.description: Policy for the offline token-hygiene checks.

isolation.description: Declared authorisation boundaries. TRUST supplies the test; the config supplies the boundary. Each spec may carry dependsOn/condition to run only when an upstream control failed.

id.description: Finding ID. It appears in the report and other specs may depend on it.

type.description: record-ownership and prefix-scoped-storage need two identities; the rest need one.

title.description: The control assertion, phrased positively. Defaults to description.

severity.description: Impact if this boundary fails. Defaults to high.

dependsOn.description: Finding ID(s) this test depends on. It runs only when the condition is met, and otherwise skips with the upstream control as the reason.

condition.description: Default: failed — run when the upstream boundary broke.

denialPatterns.description: How this API phrases a refusal. Sharpens an otherwise ambiguous verdict.

pathB.description: {id} is replaced with the record discovered as identity A.

idField.description: Field naming a record ID in identity A's response. Default: id.

idVariable.description: Variable the discovered ID is bound to in queryB. Default: id.

objectKey.description: An object under the other tenant's prefix, so reading is tested as well as listing.

identityClaimField.description: enumeration only — the field naming a record's owner. Default: owner.

identityValue.description: The caller's own identity, if the token subject is not it.

mutation.description: mutation-guard only. Runs under safety.allowDenialTests, since the control holding means nothing is written.

injectedField.description: identity-injection only — the client-supplied identity field under test.

successIndicators.description: Patterns that would appear only if the server acted on the injected identity.

idp.description: Identity-provider posture, checked unauthenticated over HTTP: discovery document, PKCE, implicit flow, client authentication, the application's own authorisation request, and a Cognito native password grant.

loginUrl.description: The application path that redirects into the IdP. Its Location header is parsed for response_type and the PKCE challenge.

web.description: Passive web surface options: sensitivePaths, redirectParams, rateLimitBurst, listingPaths, expectedFrameAncestors.

injection.description: Input-handling probe options. `body` extends the same payloads to a JSON request body, which is where a POST-first API actually takes input.

body.description: A request whose JSON fields are tested. Config-driven rather than discovered: a guessed schema returns 400 and reads as clean.

fields.description: Dotted paths into the template, e.g. "input.title".

template.description: A valid request body; each field is replaced in turn.

query.description: GraphQL document — the template is then sent as variables.

write.description: The endpoint mutates state; the probe then runs under safety.allowDenialTests.

api.description: API and authorisation probes. Also accepted as: graphql, appSync, appsync, rest, backend. api.crossService declares tokens that should be refused by a named endpoint (cross-service audience binding). api.session takes verifyEndpoint, verifyQuery (GraphQL — a document the API answers normally, so a session check reaches the auth layer instead of being rejected as malformed), verifyMethod, logoutEndpoint and expiredTokenEnv.

storage.description: Object-storage isolation probes. Also accepted as: s3, objectStore, blob, bucket.

agent.description: AI agent runtime probes. Also accepted as: agentCore, agentcore, bedrock, llm, aiAgent.

mobile.description: Mobile platform probes. Also accepted as: app, device.
